https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c74e.text: Image source, Central News and Pictures Image caption, Saad al-Hilli was shot dead with his wife and mother-in-law in September 2012 By Hugh Schofield Paris correspondent Published 4 hours ago Police investigating the unsolved murder of a British family in France 14 years ago have an unexpected new clue with the discovery of a Luger pistol in the waters of a nearby lake. One of the few certainties in the killings of Saad al-Hilli with his wife and mother-in-law â as well as a passing cyclist â is that they were shot through the head with a Luger model P06, a type used by the Swiss army until around 1960. Now France's cold case unit has confirmed the discovery of a Luger in Lake Annecy, in the Alps, not far from the scene of the murders in September 2012. According to Marianne magazine, which broke the story, it was British tourists on 20 August who found the weapon lying in two metres of water. At first they thought it was a water pistol, but realised their mistake when they felt its weight. The discovery was made near the very camping site â Le Solitaire du Lac â where the al-Hillis were staying in their caravan, Marianne reported. Forensic experts are now examining the weapon, which has been badly damaged by its time under water, to see if it is indeed a P06 model. It is estimated that around 60,000 Luger P06s were manufactured. But the number of Luger pistols in general that were made is more like three million. Exhaustive investigations in France and the UK have left police no closer to understanding who carried out the al-Hilli murders and why. Over the years a series of leads have been pursued then dropped. A British national of Iraqi birth, Saad al-Hilli was holidaying with his family in the picturesque countryside of Lake Annecy in eastern France. On the afternoon of 5 September, his body with those of his wife and mother-in-law were found in their car, its motor still running, on a forest road near the village of Chevaline. A passing cyclist had â like the other victims â been shot through the head. Poignantly, the two al-Hilli daughters, aged four and seven, survived. The older girl had been hit on the head with a pistol butt and was badly hurt. The younger, lying in the car under her mother's skirts, was not discovered till forensic experts began examining the scene many hours later. It was fragments from the pistol butt which enabled police to identify it as a Luger P06. The model is regarded more as a collector's item than a working weapon, which made the theory of a professional hit against the family seem less likely. Lake Annecy is only 50km from Switzerland, where the Luger P06 will have been familiar to older people from their military service. French police said many examples of the gun have been kept by families on either side of the border. Among the theories that have been entertained are that the murders were linked to a family row over money; that they were the work of a motiveless crank; and that the main target was the cyclist. Police were also briefly intrigued by the fact that al-Hilli's wife's first husband â an American â died of a heart attack just hours before the killings in France. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqy7.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Dozens of police and commandos were deployed to the courtroom before the verdicts were announced By Ishara Danasekara ,Â BBC Sinhala Â and Â Kumudu Jayawardana ,Â BBC Sinhala Published 22 September 2026, 13:29 BST Updated 1 hour ago Sri Lanka's High Court has given long jail sentences to 15 men charged with plotting the 2019 Easter Sunday bomb attacks that killed 270 people and injured more than 500. Those found guilty include Naufer Moulavi, who prosecutors said masterminded the suicide bombings. Nine other men were acquitted. The co-ordinated blasts at three churches and three luxury hotels were the deadliest in Sri Lanka since the end of its civil war in 2009. Forty-five foreigners were among the dead. All the bombers who carried out the attacks died in the blasts. Investigators have previously blamed the bombings on Islamist extremists, and the 25 men indicted were from Sri Lanka's Muslim minority. One died in custody. The 15 defendants on Tuesday were each given prison terms ranging from 200 to 260 years. The court in the capital Colombo also ordered the confiscation of their all movable and immovable assets. The accused, who had been charged with more than 23,000 offences, were handcuffed in pairs and brought to the court in two prison buses. Most of those killed were Sri Lankans, many of whom were children. They included celebrity chef Shantha Mayadunne and her daughter, an entire young family of five, at least eight members of staff from the hotels targeted and five members of the same family from the western Sri Lankan city of Negombo. The foreigners who died included 11 Indians, eight Britons and five Americans . Among the dead there were also citizens of Australia, Bangladesh, China, Denmark, Japan, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and Turkey. Three of Danish billionaire Anders Holch Povlsen's children died in the attack on the Shangri-La hotel, while the family had been holidaying there. 'Intelligence lapse' In the wake of the attacks, Sri Lankan authorities pointed to a "major intelligence lapse". Its parliament heard that a tip-off from India about the attacks was not properly shared with the authorities. In 2023, the Supreme Court ordered former president Maithripala Sirisena to pay millions in compensation to the victims of the bombings, after finding him responsible for national security failures that led to the attacks. Last month, two former senior officials were sentenced to death for criminal negligence that led to the bombings. Death sentences are usually commuted to life in prison in Sri Lanka due to a decades-old moratorium on executions. For years, Sri Lankans have held regular demonstrations demanding justice for the victims of the Easter attacks. The verdict comes as a separate investigation into former intelligence chief Suresh Sallay is under way. Sallay is accused of orchestrating the bombings with Islamist extremists. The allegations echo those aired in a 2023 documentary by British broadcaster Channel 4, which heard whistleblower testimony claiming the attacks were allowed to happen to boost the popularity of the Rajapaksa family, which long dominated Sri Lankan politics. Sallay, who was arrested in February, denies the allegations. Former president Gotabaya Rajapaksa, who was elected months after the 2019 attacks, with a campaign of tackling Islamist extremism has also denied the allegations. Rajapaksa, who has been banned from leaving the country, has asked the court to prevent his potential arrest in connection with the ongoing investigations. https://en.tempo.co/read/2119716/us-char.text: TEMPO.CO, Jakarta - The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has charged five men with working for Russian intelligence to carry out surveillance and plan targeted killings in the United States and Europe."The men were recruited to carry out attacks and assassinations around the world, including the United States," the DOJ said in the indictment.Yuri Khrameev, 63, and his son, Kirill Khrameev, 27, both Russian nationals; Cuban nationals Oemis Romagoza Durruthy, 35, and Yaidel Delgado Suarez, 35; and Angel Eduardo Castro of Venezuela, 22, were charged with an alleged conspiracy to commit financial terrorism.Khrameev, Suarez, and Castro were also charged with conspiracy to commit murder for hire.All the individuals are still at large.The DOJ announced the unsealing of charges against the five individuals one day after DW published an investigation looking into one of the members of the murder plot. The DW investigation identified Romagoza Durruthy as a salsa teacher in Russia who recruited a number of people in 2024 to carry out sabotage across Europe. The agents were mostly from Spanish-speaking countries and had been sent across Europe to commit arson attacks on businesses and military equipment destined for Ukraine. The investigation found that Romagoza Durruthy had been the person who directed them and organized their travels.What else did the DOJ say?Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters that the plans included attempts to assassinate a Russian dissident in Washington, DC.According to the DOJ, several people were recruited in the US alone to surveil Russian dissidents, in addition to monitoring civilian and military infrastructure in European countries such as Lithuania.The Justice Department also reported that one recruit was allegedly offered "$40,000 to 'eliminate' or 'disappear' a US resident."Last year, another recruit was allegedly offered $25,000 to kill a person living in Lithuania. Russia has previously denied carrying out such plots on foreign soil, including in the United States.The Russian Embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Read: US Bill Sanctioning Russia Could Adversely Impact IndiaClick here to get the latest news updates from Tempo on Google News

https://vietnamnews.vn/economy/1800057/v.text: Việt Nam and Poland strengthen strategic partnership in furniture supply chains HÀ NỘI — As two of the world's top three furniture exporters, Việt Nam and Poland have significant potential and opportunities to work together in furniture manufacturing supply chains. Việt Nam and Poland have furniture export turnovers of approximately US$3.7 billion and $3 billion, respectively, according to data from the trade data analytics organisation OEC. However, in addition to its furniture manufacturing and export industries, Poland also boasts a world-class industry producing machinery and equipment for forestry and wood processing. This creates considerable potential for the two countries to cooperate in developing supply chains for furniture manufacturing. Although both countries are among the world’s leading furniture producers, their furniture industries are not directly competitive due to differences in product categories and end-user markets. More importantly, their respective manufacturing capabilities offer complementary strengths that could help unlock greater cooperation potential. As a developed industrial country with a sizeable agricultural sector, Poland manufactures a wide range of advanced machinery and equipment serving the entire production process, from forestry harvesting and processing to wood manufacturing and product finishing. Polish agricultural and forestry equipment is already used in markets around the world, but remains relatively unfamiliar in Southeast Asia. Polish manufacturers hope Việt Nam can serve as a gateway for Polish products to access the wider regional market. The effective operation of Polish machinery in Việt Nam, they said, would also serve as a powerful showcase for the quality of Polish equipment across Southeast Asia. At the same time, with one of Europe’s largest areas of planted forests, Poland could potentially serve as a source of raw materials and input components for Việt Nam’s furniture industry, the Vietnam Trade Office in Poland said at a sideline forum during the international trade fair on wood and furniture industries in Poland this month. At the event, experts and enterprises from Việt Nam and Poland discussed the outlook and opportunities to promote bilateral cooperation in expanding the furniture production supply chain. Representatives of leading Polish manufacturers of agricultural and forestry machinery, including Pronar and Unia, have expressed strong interest in Việt Nam’s potential in both furniture manufacturing and mechanical engineering and manufacturing. As a result, alongside efforts to promote sales of machinery and production lines for timber harvesting and processing, these companies are also exploring opportunities to partner with Vietnamese businesses to invest in manufacturing and assembly, with a view to transferring technology for selected types of machinery serving the regional market. — VNS Economy Wood industry looks to home market for new growth Economy TCBS adopts AWS agentic AI to accelerate product development Economy Thai financial investment groups explore opportunities in Thanh Hóa Economy VN-Index fall for five days in a row Economy Hà Nội’s Q3 economic growth hits 10.02 per cent, first double-digit rise this year Economy Bắc Ninh breaks ground on expanded Việt-Hàn Industrial Park Economy Global supply chain shifts create opportunities, challenges Digitalisation and the green transition were two other long-term trends reshaping global supply chains. https://www.perthnow.com.au/news/politic.text: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs is set to retain power after a strong election win. (EPA PHOTO) Credit: AAP Latvia's PM wins election under shadow of Ukraine war Andrius Sytas and Terje Solsvik Reuters 4 October 2026, 10:04am Copy link Share story Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs is set to retain power and form a pro-Ukrainian coalition after his centrist United List secured the biggest parliamentary election victory since Latvia regained independence in 1991. With 97 per cent of ballots counted after Saturday's election in the NATO and European Union country bordering Russia, United List was on 35.3 per cent enough for 42 seats in the 100-seat parliament. A businessman and amateur rally driver, Kulbergs, 47, came to power in May after the previous coalition crumbled over its handling of incidents in which stray Ukrainian military drones flew undetected into Latvia. Latvia's economy has underperformed its Baltic neighbours for more than a decade and Kulbergs has vowed to improve governance, cut red tape and reduce public spending. United List appears able to secure a parliamentary majority with either the nationalist National Alliance or the liberal Progressives. Kulbergs pledged continuing support to Ukraine and to keep a hard line towards Moscow. "Any economic ties with Russia makes us weak. Yes, it can bring some extra money, but it's a weakness Russia might exploit," he told reporters at his party's headquarters on election night as supporters celebrated the scale of the win. "It's remarkably good. I was not expecting such a result." Voter turnout was 51.8 per cent down from 59.4 per cent in 2022. United List was followed by the populist, MAGA-style Latvia First, which was on 13.1 per cent. Latvia First had courted the country's substantial ethnic Russian minority in the run-up to the vote. Third in the ranking was the pro-Russian Sovereign Power party, on 11.7 per cent followed by the National Alliance, which promotes a hardline approach to the Kremlin, at 8.9 per cent. Throughout his campaign, Kulbergs promised more anti-drone capability for Latvia and to maintain defence spending at five per cent of gross domestic product, one of the highest levels in NATO. His pro-Kremlin rivals said Latvia should stop any aid to Ukraine and instead focus on tackling cost-of-living issues, particularly among the country's Russian-speaking minority. Although pro-Russian parties increased their representation, Kits said they remained sidelined and were unlikely to influence government policy. Latvia's ethnic Russian minority is split between those who oppose Moscow's war in Ukraine and others who voice frustration with policies at home aimed at limiting their influence on public life, which many of them see as discriminatory. Latvia, with a population of 1.9 million, is sandwiched between the Baltic Sea and Russia and Belarus to the east, with EU and NATO allies Estonia and Lithuania to the north and south.
